div.note: Liebermann compares Norðleod 9 and 11.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘That of a mass-thegn ["a priest in full orders"] and a secular thegn 2,000 thrymsas.’).
i.e. a priest in full orders; cf. mœssepreost

If a thryms is equal to three pence, 2,000 would give the thegn a 1,200 shilling wergild, reckoning 5 pence to the shilling, as in Wessex; yet in the next chapter 266 thrymsas gives the ceorl a 200 (actually 199 ) shilling wergild only if 4 pence are reckoned to the shilling. Thus the normal relationship of 1:6 between the wergilds of ceorl and thegn is upset.
